Topic: How to answer when clients ask about AI
Full Post Copy:
'Can we do something about ChatGPT?'

Your clients are going to ask this. Some already have.

SEO might not be your first specialism—and that's ok.

Most agencies fumble it:
→ 'We're watching this space' (translation: no idea)
→ 'It's too early to tell' (translation: haven't looked into it)
→ 'Focus on what's working' (translation: please change the subject)

Here's what to say instead:

'Yes—and we can help.'

Then explain it simply:

'When people ask AI for recommendations, it pulls from reviews, forums, and third-party mentions more than your website. There are specific things we can do to make sure you show up in those answers.'

That's it. No jargon. No 'AEO' or 'GEO' or 'LLMO.'

Just: 'People are asking AI for recommendations. Here's how we get you mentioned.'

Then offer a next step:

'We can run a quick audit to see where you stand right now. Takes 30 minutes. We'll show you exactly what AI says about your business—and your competitors.'

You don't need to be an AI expert.

You need to be more confident than your client.

Here's the thing though:

Traditional SEO still matters more than ever. Google is still 20x bigger than ChatGPT. The fundamentals—rankings, content, technical health—aren't going anywhere.

AI visibility builds ON your SEO. It doesn't replace it.

The smartest agencies are doing both.

Rand Fishkin's team ran 2,961 identical prompts through ChatGPT, Claude, and Google AI.

The result?

Less than 1 in 100 chance you'll get the same brand list twice.

One hospital appeared in 97% of responses—but ranked #1 only 36% of the time.

What this means:

You can't optimise for a metric that changes every single query.

The vendors selling 'Position #1 in ChatGPT' will quietly drop the service in six months when more firms realise the data is meaningless.

So what DO you focus on?

→ Citation frequency (are you showing up?)
→ How you're described (what do they say about you?)
→ Traditional SEO (LLMs query search engines before answering)

The play isn't ranking position.

It's being in the conversation—and being described well when you are.

Stop chasing phantom rankings. Start building real presence.

Topic: LinkedIn posts appear in AI within hours
Full Post Copy:
LinkedIn posts can appear in AI search within hours.

Sometimes minutes.

Especially for accounts with strong followings.

Reddit and YouTube show similar behaviour.

This changes the game for agencies.

Your clients don't need to wait 6 months for SEO to 'kick in' to influence AI visibility.

They can publish today and show up in AI answers tomorrow.

The tactics:

→ Post consistently on LinkedIn (company + personal)
→ Answer real questions your customers ask
→ Repurpose across Reddit, YouTube, and niche forums
→ Build the 'digital gossip' that LLMs pull from

AI visibility isn't just about your website anymore.

It's about showing up in all the places LLMs look.

Social works fast. Use it.

Topic: Good AEO is still good SEO
Full Post Copy:
John Mueller said it directly at Google Search Live:

'AI systems rely on search. There is no such thing as GEO or AEO without doing SEO fundamentals.'

'Tricks will come out and they will work for a short time. Companies that want to be around for the long term should focus on something that is proven with long term stability and not tricks.'

This is the thing most 'AI SEO' vendors don't want you to hear.

Modern LLMs use Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).

They query search engines in real time before answering.

If you want LLM visibility, you need to show up in search first.

The shortcut everyone wants doesn't exist.

The path that works:

→ Clean technical foundations
→ Content that answers real questions
→ Proprietary data and original research
→ Distribution that builds brand recognition

Traditional SEO isn't dead. It's the foundation everything else sits on.

Good AEO is still good SEO.

Stop tracking phantom rankings.

Rand's research proves it: you'll get cited sometimes, not always.

Randomisation is extreme.

One hospital appeared in 97% of AI responses—but ranked #1 only 36% of the time.

Less than 1 in 100 chance you'll get the same brand list twice.

So what DO you measure?

Citation frequency: How often are you showing up?
Brand sentiment: How are you being described when you do?
Source diversity: Are you appearing across multiple LLMs?

The play isn't 'rank #1 in ChatGPT.'

It's being in the conversation—consistently, across platforms.

The vendors selling 'Position #1 in ChatGPT' will quietly drop the service in six months.

Tell your clients the truth. Build something real.
